caption: How a hi team works. People talk to the lead in the team's Slack channel or a DM, and send feedback from the helper on the app's pages; the lead, Hermes, helps them and files what they ask for as tasks. The owners build in the dev box, a long-lived box with the project, Claude Code, Codex, and herdr, reached over SSH or from the dev page in a browser. Work leaves the box through the team's service, part of hi on the machine: hi dev preview puts a branch on the preview, and hi dev ship merges it into dev. Production moves only when an owner releases dev from the dev page, with a snapshot first. Everything lives in the team's folder.
via: the Slack channel · the helper · the dev page

key.text: One team, one Slack channel, one machine. People reach the app through its links; owners reach the dev box over NetBird or the dev page.
The one agent that runs all the time; it talks with the people and files what they ask for, and never writes code.
Where the owners and their agents build; the agents ask no permissions, since the box is the boundary.
Part of hi, outside every box: the dev box can preview and ship through it, but nothing it offers moves production.
What the people try, and what they use. Only an owner's click moves production.
Everything the team knows and has made, to back up, restore, or move.
